mapping.formal_value: candidate-1, candidate-2 (distinct primitive ids, identical content)
mapping.concrete_e1: table candidates, two rows whose content-addressed ids differ; value/record/field/producer/selection artifact/expected version/evidence content are equal
mapping.note: Concrete identity is content-addressed over 17 fields including created_at (app/domain/authority.py:251-273), so a pair that is byte-identical except for its identity cannot coexist (Phase 1 R1).
field name only; no semantic role of the name is used.

mapping.concrete_e1: candidates.evidence_hash (content) + candidates.evidence_locator (storage handle). Variant (a): both hashes coincide. Variant (b): hashes differ.
mapping.note: The formal model has one evidence identifier, i.e. variant (a). Variant (b) is the unfavourable case required by the unverified PNG-encoding question (O1).

mapping.concrete_e1: Full: decisions (candidate_id) + authorization_bindings (certificate_id, authorized value). B1/B2/B2+: approvals (principal, record, expected version, authorized values) with no candidate reference.
mapping.correspondence: exact for Full, deliberately reduced for B1/B2
mapping.note: The reduction is the semantic difference under test (sections 6, 9).

mapping.formal_value: batch_items[*].candidate_id (candidate-1 in SAFE, candidate-2 in UNSAFE)
mapping.concrete_e1: the candidate handle passed to submit(); never persisted by B1/B2/B2+
mapping.note: It is the only input that varies between the two histories (section 37).

mapping.formal_value: normative_outcome = [admissible, complete-successor, complete-trace] in SAFE; differs in UNSAFE
mapping.concrete_e1: observed.accepted/reason plus the successor state in records, versions, audits, fact_sources
mapping.note: The formal outcome is a three-element trace predicate; the concrete outcome is accept/reject plus the persisted successor.

mapping.concrete_e1: declared semantic projection of the SAFE and UNSAFE post-states

boundaries: E1 is an analogue of the formal additional identity pair, not a proof that byte-identical duplicate certificates exist in production.

The concrete identity pair is a baseline-observation-equivalent pair: the two candidates differ only in fields that no baseline-visible observation depends on, and additionally in evidence content in the unfavourable variant (b).

No production identity scheme, uniqueness constraint or case was modified to construct the pair; the pair is generated through the ordinary candidate-recording path (two record_candidate() calls, Phase 1 section 13.2).
